CDK4/6 inhibitors are used in hormone-receptor-positive breast cancers to block cell cycle progression at G1.
VEGF inhibitors (like bevacizumab) act on angiogenesis; RAS status does not currently determine their use in colon cancer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In the TNM staging system used for clinical classification of malignancies, what specific parameter is represented by the 'T' component?
options: The total number of regional lymph nodes involved
The presence of microscopic vascular invasion
The number of distant organ sites involved
The size or depth of invasion of the primary tumor
correctOption: The size or depth of invasion of the primary tumor
optionExplanations: Tumor grade (differentiation) is separate from clinical staging (TNM).
The number of involved regional lymph nodes is defined by the 'N' (Nodal) component.
Microscopic vascular invasion is a pathological feature but not the primary definition of the 'T' stage.
The number of distant organ sites is part of the 'M' (Metastatic) component.
The 'T' parameter specifically classifies the primary tumor based on its physical size or how deeply it has invaded local structures.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page): [T] Increase in primary tumour size or depth of invasion

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 68-year-old patient with metastatic lung cancer is evaluated for fitness for systemic therapy. The patient is capable of all self-care and is ambulatory but is unable to carry out any work activities. They spend approximately 4 hours of their 16-hour waking day resting in bed. What is the correct Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score for this patient?
optionExplanations: Score 0 indicates the patient is fully active and can carry on all pre-disease performance without restriction.
Score 1 indicates the patient is restricted in strenuous activity but can do light work.
Score 2 defines a patient who is ambulatory and capable of self-care but unable to work, and is awake/active for more than 50% of the day.
Score 4 indicates the patient is completely disabled and totally confined to a bed or chair.
Score 3 indicates the patient is capable of only limited self-care and is confined to a bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): 2 Ambulatory and capable of all self-care but unable to work. Up and about more than 50% of waking hours

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Diagnostic Approach to Cancer of Unknown Primary
statement: A 30-year-old male presents with multiple pulmonary nodules and a bulky retroperitoneal mass on CT. He has no history of primary cancer. Which of the following sets of investigations is most appropriate to help identify a 'favorable' subset of cancer of unknown primary (CUP) that might be curable with chemotherapy in this specific demographic?
optionExplanations: CA-125 and pelvic imaging are the primary workup for suspected ovarian cancer in women.
Colonoscopy and CEA are appropriate for suspected gastrointestinal primaries, typically seen in older patients with different patterns of spread.
PSA and bone scans are utilized for suspected prostate cancer, usually in older men with blastic bone lesions.
Mammography is indicated for women with axillary nodes, not young men with midline/retroperitoneal disease.
In young men with midline disease (retroperitoneal/mediastinal), checking germ cell markers (AFP/hCG) is vital to identify highly treatable extragonadal germ cell tumors.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 139 (Book Page): [CUP – favourable] Men with poorly differentiated carcinoma with midline distribution [Management] Treat like germ cell cancer... [Page 139 (Book Page) Box 7.11] α-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) in midline disease in young men

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Biochemical Markers of Tumor Lysis Syndrome
statement: A 65-year-old male with bulky high-grade lymphoma begins his first cycle of intensive cytotoxic chemotherapy. The oncology team monitors him closely for Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS). According to standard biochemical monitoring, which of the following is usually the earliest marker to elevate following significant malignant cell destruction?
optionExplanations: Creatinine rises later as a consequence of renal impairment from uric acid crystal precipitation.
ALT is a marker of hepatocyte injury and is not a core component of the metabolic derangements seen in TLS.
Serum calcium typically decreases (hypocalcemia) in TLS due to precipitation with high levels of phosphate.
Potassium is an intracellular ion; its release during rapid cell lysis makes hyperkalemia the earliest biochemical indicator of TLS.
Serum albumin is a marker of nutrition and chronicity; it does not rise during acute tumor lysis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): Elevated serum potassium may be the earliest biochemical marker [of tumour lysis syndrome]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: During the performance of a fine needle aspiration (FNA) of a palpable neck mass, the clinician is instructed to halt the procedure immediately if a specific finding is observed. What is the primary reason to stop sampling during the aspiration phase?
options: Blood is seen in the syringe hub
Negative pressure is lost in the syringe
correctOption: Blood is seen in the syringe hub
optionExplanations: The presence of blood in the syringe hub contaminates the cytological sample and significantly reduces its diagnostic quality/clarity.
Mild discomfort is expected; local anesthetic can be used, but it is not a reason to stop the sampling itself.
Loss of negative pressure would stop the aspiration of cells, but the clinical directive specifically emphasizes stopping if blood contamination occurs.
Varying the angles (fan-out technique) is actually a recommended part of the procedure to get an adequate sample.
The lesion should be immobilized; if it moves, the operator should re-fix it rather than stop the procedure entirely.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): Stop sampling if blood is seen in the syringe hub as blood reduces the quality of the sample.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A clinical stage is assigned to a cancer patient following an initial workup. In the internationally recognized TNM staging system, what specific parameter is the 'N' component designed to evaluate?
options: The presence or absence of distant metastatic spread.
The metabolic activity of the tumor on molecular scans.
The size and local extent of the primary tumor mass.
The degree of cellular differentiation on microscopy.
The status of involvement of regional lymph nodes.
correctOption: The status of involvement of regional lymph nodes.
optionExplanations: This describes the M (Metastasis) component, indicating spread to distant organs.
Metabolic activity is an investigative finding (often via PET) but not a standard TNM category definition.
This describes the T (Tumor) component, which evaluates the primary mass size or depth.
This refers to the histological grade of the tumor, which is separate from TNM staging.
Correct. The N component specifically refers to the involvement and extent of regional lymph nodes.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page): One of the most commonly used systems is the T (tumour), N (regional lymph nodes), M (metastatic sites) approach of the International Union against Cancer (UICC, see Box 7.3).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A medical oncologist is reviewing imaging options for a patient with suspected metastatic disease. What is the fundamental physiological principle that allows Positron Emission Tomography (PET) to distinguish malignant tissues from surrounding normal structures?
options: Reflection of high-frequency sound waves off tissue borders.
Identification of vascular permeability and blood flow rates.
Measurement of the differential absorption of ionizing X-rays.
Detection of hydrogen proton density and relaxation times.
Visualization of the metabolic activity of tumor cells.
correctOption: Visualization of the metabolic activity of tumor cells.
optionExplanations: This describes the mechanism of Ultrasound imaging.
While PET can sometimes evaluate perfusion, its primary diagnostic use in oncology is assessing metabolic activity.
This is the principle of Computed Tomography (CT) and standard radiography.
This is the principle behind Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), not PET.
Correct. PET utilizes radiopharmaceuticals to visualize the high metabolic rate (glucose uptake) characteristic of most cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In the staging and diagnostic workup of malignancies, certain imaging modalities are preferred for specific anatomical regions due to superior resolution. For which of the following areas is Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) considered the preferred diagnostic technique?
options: Assessment of the abdomen for bowel obstruction.
Detection of small pleural effusions in the chest.
Evaluation of the thorax for pulmonary nodules.
Staging of rectal, cervical, and prostate cancers.
Screening of the liver for early cirrhosis changes.
correctOption: Staging of rectal, cervical, and prostate cancers.
optionExplanations: Standard radiographs or CT are typically used for acute abdominal issues like obstruction.
Ultrasound is highly sensitive and preferred for identifying and guiding drainage of pleural effusions.
CT is generally preferred for thoracic imaging and lung nodule detection.
Correct. MRI is the gold standard for pelvic imaging, including rectal and gynecological malignancies.
Ultrasound or CT are more common for liver screening, though MRI is used for specific lesion characterization.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. It is widely employed for the staging of rectal, cervical and prostate cancers.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 68-year-old male with a 40-pack-year smoking history presents with a two-week history of worsening breathlessness and facial fullness. On physical examination, his face appears plethoric and cyanosed, with visible distension of the neck and upper chest wall veins. His jugular venous pulse is elevated and non-pulsatile. What is the most appropriate investigation of choice to confirm the suspected diagnosis and differentiate between extrinsic compression and intravascular causes?
options: Computed Tomography (CT) scan of the thorax.
Endoscopic Bronchial Ultrasound with fine needle biopsy.
Transthoracic Echocardiogram to evaluate right heart pressure.
Magnetic Resonance Angiography of the upper vasculature.
Chest Radiograph (X-ray) in the posterior-anterior view.
correctOption: Computed Tomography (CT) scan of the thorax.
optionExplanations: Correct. CT of the thorax is the standard for diagnosing Superior Vena Cava Obstruction (SVCO) and identifying the cause.
EBUS-FNA is a staging/biopsy tool but not the initial diagnostic choice for the vascular obstruction itself.
Echocardiography assesses the heart but is not the definitive test for diagnosing the site and nature of SVC blockage.
MRA is useful but not the primary investigation of choice compared to contrast-enhanced CT.
A chest X-ray may show a mass but cannot reliably differentiate between extrinsic compression and thrombus in SVCO.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 143 (Book Page): The investigation of choice is a CT scan of the thorax to confirm the diagnosis and distinguish between extra- and intravascular causes.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Biochemical markers are frequently utilized in oncology, though they require careful interpretation. The elevation of Carcinoembryonic Antigen (CEA) is most significantly associated with which clinical finding in patients with gastrointestinal malignancy?
options: Presence of localized early-stage gastric carcinoma.
Initial screening for benign colonic adenomatous polyps.
Development of colorectal cancer with liver metastasis.
Diagnosis of primary hepatocellular cancer in smokers.
Differentiation between ulcerative colitis and Crohn's.
correctOption: Development of colorectal cancer with liver metastasis.
optionExplanations: CEA is not sensitive enough for early-stage localized gastric cancer diagnosis.
Tumor markers are generally not recommended for screening asymptomatic individuals for polyps.
Correct. CEA is a high-yield marker for colorectal cancer, especially when there is hepatic involvement.
Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is the marker associated with hepatocellular carcinoma, not CEA.
CEA can be elevated in inflammatory conditions like ulcerative colitis, but it does not differentiate between IBD types.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA)... Elevated in colorectal cancer, particularly with liver metastasis, gastric cancer, breast cancer, lung cancer, mucinous cancer of the ovary.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A patient is evaluated for fitness before beginning a rigorous regimen of systemic anti-cancer therapy. If the patient is capable of only limited self-care and is confined to a bed or chair for 60% of their waking hours, what is their score on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status scale?
optionExplanations: Correct. Grade 3 is defined as being confined to a bed or chair for more than 50% of waking hours.
Grade 4 signifies a completely disabled patient, totally confined to a bed or chair.
Grade 1 signifies a patient restricted in strenuous activity but ambulatory and able to work.
Grade 2 signifies a patient ambulatory and capable of self-care but up and about more than 50% of waking hours.
Grade 0 signifies a fully active patient with no restrictions.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): 3 Capable of only limited self-care, confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA) is a common method for obtaining cellular material from a suspected malignant lesion. According to standard procedural guidelines, what action should the operator take immediately once the needle tip has entered the edge of the lesion?
options: Apply negative pressure by pulling on the syringe.
Rotate the needle 360 degrees to shear the tissue.
Withdraw the needle completely to check the hub.
Release all pressure to allow capillary action fill.
Inject a small volume of saline to loosen cells.
correctOption: Apply negative pressure by pulling on the syringe.
optionExplanations: Correct. Negative pressure is applied once the tip is in the lesion to suck cells into the needle.
While rotation occurs, the critical next step described is the application of negative pressure.
The needle should not be withdrawn until the sampling passes are completed.
Negative pressure must be maintained during the passes and only released before withdrawal.
Saline injection is not part of the standard FNA technique for sampling palpable masses.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): When the needle tip is at the edge of the lesion, apply negative pressure by pulling on the syringe and continue to enter the lesion.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 52-year-old male presents with a single, enlarged, painless squamous cell carcinoma node in the cervical region. Extensive clinical examination, naso-endoscopy, and initial imaging fail to identify a primary site. What is the most appropriate next investigative step to evaluate for a potential primary source or additional sites of disease?
options: Serum measurement of Alpha-fetoprotein and hCG.
Random blind biopsies of the contralateral tonsil.
Repeat Computed Tomography of the abdomen and pelvis.
optionExplanations: Laparoscopy is used for abdominal/peritoneal malignancies, not for localized neck disease.
AFP and hCG are markers for germ cell tumors, not typical for squamous cell carcinoma of the neck.
Blind biopsies are low yield compared to functional imaging when endoscopy is negative.
Correct. PET scans are indicated for squamous neck nodes when the primary is not found on endoscopy.
If CT thorax/abdomen/pelvis was already done in the initial workup, a repeat is not the next logical step.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 139 (Book Page): PET scan for single-site disease or squamous neck nodes with no primary on endoscopic evaluation.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Immunohistochemical (IHC) staining of biopsy specimens is pivotal for tailoring cancer treatment. What is the primary clinical significance of finding Oestrogen (ER) and Progesterone (PR) receptor positivity in a breast cancer specimen?
options: It identifies the tumor as being highly sensitive to alkylating agents.
It predicts a high likelihood of response to HER2 inhibitors.
It suggests the cancer is sensitive to hormonal manipulation.
It indicates a poor prognosis with resistance to all therapies.
It confirms that the tumor is of a basal-like genetic subtype.
correctOption: It suggests the cancer is sensitive to hormonal manipulation.
optionExplanations: IHC markers for receptors do not directly predict sensitivity to non-specific cytotoxic alkylating agents.
HER2 status is independent of ER/PR and predicts response to HER2 inhibitors like trastuzumab.
Correct. ER/PR positivity guides the use of anti-oestrogen therapies (e.g., tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors).
ER/PR positivity is generally a favorable prognostic factor compared to triple-negative disease.
Basal-like (triple-negative) tumors are characteristically ER, PR, and HER2 negative.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): Oestrogen (ER) and progesterone (PR) receptor positivity indicate that the cancer may be sensitive to hormonal manipulation.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: During the histopathological evaluation of a tumor sample, the presence of specific cellular morphologies can provide clues regarding the primary site of the malignancy. The identification of 'signet-ring cells' most strongly favors which primary site?
optionExplanations: Ovarian cancer is more commonly associated with psammoma bodies and mucin production.
Renal cancer typically shows clear cell or papillary morphology.
Melanoma is identified by the presence of melanin and specific IHC markers like S100 or HMB-45.
Correct. Signet-ring cell carcinoma is a classic histological variant of gastric cancer.
Thyroid cancer is often associated with psammoma bodies or specific nuclear features, not signet-ring cells.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 52-year-old woman with metastatic ovarian cancer undergoes a follow-up computed tomography scan three months after starting chemotherapy. The radiologist notes that the sum of the longest diameters of the target lesions has decreased by exactly 35% compared to the baseline measurement. According to the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (RECIST), how should this patient's treatment response be classified?
optionExplanations: Complete response requires the total disappearance of all target lesions, not just a 35% reduction.
Partial response is correctly defined as a minimum 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameters of target lesions.
Progressive disease requires a 20% increase in the sum of the diameters or the appearance of new lesions.
Mixed clinical response is not a formal category within the standard RECIST criteria used for solid tumor evaluation.
Stable disease is defined as response that does not show sufficient shrinkage to qualify for partial response nor a sufficient increase for progressive disease.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 148 (Book Page): [Partial response (PR) At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameter (LD) of target lesions, taking as reference the baseline sum LD]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 64-year-old patient with known squamous cell carcinoma of the lung presents with confusion, polyuria, and severe constipation. Laboratory results confirm a serum calcium level of 3.2 mmol/L. Which metabolic mechanism is most likely responsible for this finding in 80% of patients with this metabolic disorder in malignancy?
options: Ectopic secretion of native parathyroid hormone
Direct invasion of the bone by tumor metastases
Reduced renal clearance of circulating calcium ions
optionExplanations: Ectopic PTH secretion is a rare mechanism and does not represent the common cause of hypercalcemia in cancer.
Parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP) production is the dominant mechanism (80%) in hypercalcemia of malignancy.
Direct bone invasion (osteolytic metastases) accounts for approximately 20% of hypercalcemia cases, not the majority.
Excessive vitamin D production is seen in some lymphomas but is not the primary mechanism in 80% of oncology cases.
While PTHrP does increase renal reabsorption, the primary classified mechanism is its over-production mimicking PTH action.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): [It is most commonly due to over-production of PTHrP (80%), which binds to the PTH receptor and elevates serum calcium by stimulating osteoclastic bone resorption]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 68-year-old man presents with suspected localized recurrence of prostate cancer following radical therapy. Which imaging modality is currently recognized as the preferred technique for evaluating the pelvic region and bone involvement in this clinical scenario?
optionExplanations: Ultrasonography is useful for solid organ lesions like liver or kidney but not for staging pelvic prostate recurrence.
MRI is explicitly stated as the preferred technique for brain, bone, and pelvic imaging due to high resolution.
PET is used to assess metabolic activity and distant metastases but is not the primary preferred pelvic imaging tool.
Isotope bone scans are sensitive for detecting metastases but MRI is superior for detailed anatomical pelvic evaluation.
Computed tomography is useful for the thorax and abdomen but lacks the resolution of MRI for pelvic structures.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): [Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 58-year-old female with advanced breast cancer presents with sharp back pain that worsens when coughing or lying flat. Examination reveals symmetrical leg weakness, increased knee jerks, and a sensory level at the T10 dermatome. She also reports recent urinary retention. Which anatomical pattern of neurological deficit is most consistent with these findings?
optionExplanations: Spinal cord compression is characterized by symmetrical weakness, increased reflexes (UMN signs), a clear sensory level, and late sphincter loss.
Conus medullaris compression usually presents with very early sphincter loss and mixed reflex signs rather than a clear sensory level.
Cauda equina typically presents with asymmetrical weakness and decreased reflexes, which contradicts the symmetrical increased jerks here.
Peripheral polyneuropathy would present with distal, glove-and-stocking sensory loss and decreased reflexes.
Lambert-Eaton is a paraneoplastic neuromuscular junction disorder presenting with proximal weakness, not a sensory level and sphincter loss.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 140 (Book Page): [The earliest sign is back pain... Subsequent ly, sensory changes develop in dermatomes below the level of compression, and motor weakness distal to the block occurs... Physical examination findings consistent with an upper motor neuron lesion]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Biochemical Markers in Tumor Lysis Syndrome
statement: A 25-year-old male with bulky mediastinal lymphoma is about to start aggressive cytotoxic chemotherapy. The oncology team monitors his biochemical markers closely to identify early signs of tumor lysis syndrome. Which pre-treatment laboratory value correlates most strongly with total tumor bulk and serves as an indicator of increased risk for this syndrome?
optionExplanations: Phosphate rise occurs during the syndrome but is not used as the primary pre-treatment risk stratification marker.
Uric acid rise is a consequence of nucleic acid breakdown during the syndrome, not the initial bulk predictor.
Potassium rises during TLS as cells are destroyed, but it is not the primary pre-treatment indicator of total bulk.
Hypocalcaemia is a clinical feature of the syndrome, but baseline calcium does not predict tumor bulk.
LDH is a marker of cell turnover and total tumor volume, specifically identified as a risk indicator for TLS.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): [pre-treatment serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) correlates with tumour bulk and may indicate increased risk.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: An 80-year-old woman is being assessed for her suitability for palliative chemotherapy for gastric cancer. She is currently able to perform all her self-care activities and is up and about for approximately 10 hours of her 16 waking hours. However, she feels too fatigued to continue her part-time office work. What is her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score?
optionExplanations: Grade 0 signifies a fully active patient who can carry on all usual activities without restriction.
Grade 4 signifies a completely disabled patient totally confined to bed or chair.
Grade 1 applies to patients restricted in strenuous activity but able to carry out light work.
Grade 3 signifies a patient capable of only limited self-care and confined to bed or chair for more than 50% of waking hours.
Grade 2 is defined as being capable of self-care and ambulatory but unable to work, remaining up for more than 50% of waking hours.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): [2 Ambulatory and capable of all self-care but unable to work. Up and about more than 50% of waking hours]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A patient with a metastatic adenocarcinoma of unknown primary origin undergoes a biopsy of a liver lesion. Immunohistochemical (IHC) staining reveals the tumor cells are CK20 positive, CK7 negative, and CDX2 positive. Based on this specific IHC profile, which primary cancer site should be prioritized for treatment planning?
optionExplanations: The CK20+, CK7-, and CDX2+ profile is pathognomonic for a colorectal origin in IHC analysis.
Gastroesophageal cancers typically show different cytokeratin patterns and are less specifically associated with this exact triple profile.
Pancreatic cancers are frequently CK7 positive, which excludes the profile described.
Pulmonary adenocarcinomas are typically CK7 positive and CK20 negative, the opposite of this profile.
Ovarian cancers are generally CK7 positive and would not typically express this specific colorectal marker set.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 139 (Book Page): [Adenocarcinoma with a colorectal-IHC prole (CK20 + , CK7 , CDX2 + ) Treat like colon cancer]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Diagnosis of Superior Vena Cava Obstruction
statement: A 65-year-old man with a 40-pack-year smoking history presents with a two-week history of worsening breathlessness and facial swelling. On examination, he has distended non-pulsatile neck veins and dilated collateral vessels across his upper chest wall. He appears plethoric. Which investigation is recognized as the initial choice to confirm this diagnosis and differentiate between extrinsic compression and intravascular thrombosis?
optionExplanations: While MRV can see vessels, CT thorax is the established primary choice for rapid diagnosis and staging of the cause of SVCO.
CT scan of the thorax is the preferred investigation to confirm SVCO and determine if the cause is extrinsic (tumor) or intrinsic (thrombus).
Doppler of the neck may show jugular distension but cannot evaluate the site of obstruction within the mediastinum.
V/Q scans are used for pulmonary embolism, not for diagnosing superior vena cava obstruction.
Echocardiography can visualize the heart but is not the gold standard for evaluating the superior vena cava in this context.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 141 (Book Page): [The investigation of choice is a CT scan of the thorax to conrm the diagnosis and distinguish between extra- and intravascular causes.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: MASCC Risk Index for Febrile Neutropenia
statement: A patient receiving cytotoxic chemotherapy for breast cancer presents to the emergency department with a single oral temperature reading of 38.4°C. Her absolute neutrophil count is determined to be 0.4 x 10^9/L. Which additional risk factor is specifically included in the MASCC risk index score to help determine if she can be managed as a low-risk outpatient?
options: Presence of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Type of cytotoxic chemotherapy agent used
Primary tumor stage at time of diagnosis
correctOption: Presence of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
optionExplanations: The absence of COPD is a specific criteria in the MASCC score, awarding 4 points toward a low-risk status.
The specific chemotherapy agent is not part of the score; the score focuses on the patient's clinical physiological state.
Hemoglobin levels are not a parameter used in the MASCC risk index calculation.
Tumor stage is not part of the MASCC score, though the type of tumor (solid vs. hematological) is considered.
General admission history is not used; the score focuses on the burden of the current illness and specific comorbidities.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 141 (Book Page): [Score 21 = low risk febrile neutropenia... Characteristic: No chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (Score 4)]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Tumor Markers for Germ Cell Tumors
statement: A 22-year-old male presents with a large midline mediastinal mass detected on a routine chest radiograph. Clinical suspicion for a germ-cell tumor is high. Which pair of biochemical tumor markers is most appropriate to assist in the diagnosis and monitoring of this patient?
optionExplanations: AFP and hCG are the classic biochemical markers used to diagnose and monitor germ-cell tumors, including testicular and midline varieties.
CEA and CA-19.9 are primarily markers for gastrointestinal and pancreatic malignancies, not germ-cell tumors.
CA-125 is used for ovarian cancer, and Thyroglobulin is used for monitoring differentiated thyroid cancers.
Beta-2-microglobulin is a marker for myeloma and lymphoma; while PLAP can be elevated in germ cell tumors, AFP/hCG are the primary clinical pair.
PSA is specific to the prostate, and Calcitonin is a marker for medullary thyroid cancer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): [Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) favour germ-cell tumours.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Which term best describes the clinical process used to determine the size of a primary tumor and whether it has spread to regional lymph nodes or distant sites?
optionExplanations: Tumor differentiation profiling refers to assessing how much the tumor resembles normal tissue, which is related to grading, not staging.
Grading refers to the microscopic appearance and aggressiveness of cells, whereas staging refers to the physical extent and spread of the disease.
Clonal expansion describes the biological growth process of malignant cells rather than the clinical investigation of disease extent.
Cytogenetic hybridization (like FISH) is a laboratory technique used to detect chromosomal abnormalities, not the overall extent of disease.
Staging is the standardized process of evaluating the tumor size (T), nodal involvement (N), and metastasis (M) to guide treatment and prognosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 133 (Book Page): [The extent of disease, such as how large a tumour is and if it has spread, is determined by the process of staging.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A patient undergoes a combined Positron Emission Tomography and Computed Tomography (PET-CT) scan. What is the primary physiological mechanism that allows PET to complement the anatomical data provided by CT?
options: Measurement of acoustic impedance in solid organ lesions
Visualization of high metabolic activity within tumor cells
Assessment of vascular permeability using iodine contrast
Identification of radioactive seed decay in pelvic organs
Detection of hydrogen proton resonance in adipose tissues
correctOption: Visualization of high metabolic activity within tumor cells
optionExplanations: Acoustic impedance is the principle behind ultrasound imaging, which measures how sound waves travel through different tissue densities.
PET scans utilize radiopharmaceuticals like FDG to identify areas of increased glucose metabolism, which is characteristic of most malignant cells.
Vascular permeability assessment using iodine is a feature of contrast-enhanced CT, not the functional metabolic imaging of PET.
Radioactive seed decay is associated with brachytherapy treatment and is not the diagnostic mechanism for PET imaging.
Hydrogen proton resonance is the basis for Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), not Positron Emission Tomography.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): [Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 62-year-old male is suspected of having a localized rectal malignancy. Which imaging modality is preferred for staging this specific site due to its high resolution in pelvic and bone imaging?
optionExplanations: CT is excellent for thoracic and abdominal staging (detecting distant spread) but is inferior to MRI for localized pelvic soft tissue resolution.
MRI provides superior soft-tissue contrast, making it the gold standard for staging cancers in the pelvis, including rectal and prostate malignancies.
Isotope bone scans detect osteoblastic activity (metastases) but cannot be used to stage the primary rectal tumor itself.
Barium enemas visualize the lumen but do not provide the necessary cross-sectional information for staging the depth of tumor invasion.
Ultrasound is useful for liver or kidney lesions but lacks the resolution required for detailed local staging of rectal wall invasion.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): [Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. It is widely employed for the staging of rectal, cervical and prostate cancers.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 68-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of a persistent cough, hemoptysis, and a 10 kg weight loss. She is currently able to perform all self-care but is unable to carry out any work activities and spends approximately 30% of her waking hours resting in bed. Physical examination reveals dullness to percussion at the right lung base. A CT scan confirms a 4 cm mass in the right lower lobe and multiple lesions in the liver. Based on the standard oncology scales, how should her functional status be classified?
optionExplanations: ECOG 3 describes a patient capable of only limited self-care who is confined to a bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours.
The patient is capable of self-care but unable to work and is up more than 50% of the time (resting 30%), which fits the criteria for ECOG 2.
ECOG 0 refers to a patient who is fully active and able to carry on all pre-disease performance without restriction.
ECOG 4 describes a completely disabled patient who cannot carry out any self-care and is totally confined to a bed or chair.
ECOG 1 applies to patients restricted in physically strenuous activity but ambulatory and able to carry out light or sedentary work.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): [2 Ambulatory and capable of all self-care but unable to work. Up and about more than 50% of waking hours]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A clinician monitors a patient with suspected pancreatic cancer. Laboratory results show a significantly elevated Cancer Antigen 19.9 (CA-19.9). Which physiological condition must be excluded to ensure this elevation is not a false positive due to impaired marker elimination?
optionExplanations: Because CA-19.9 is eliminated exclusively through the biliary tract, any blockage (cholestasis) will lead to its accumulation and a false-positive rise.
Heart failure can cause a rise in CA-125 due to serosal effusions, but it does not specifically impair the elimination of CA-19.9.
Thyrotoxicosis affects metabolic rate but has no direct impact on the biliary excretion of CA-19.9 markers.
Beta-2-microglobulin is affected by renal disease, but CA-19.9 is eliminated via the bile, not the kidneys.
Pulmonary fibrosis is not a recognized cause for the elevation of the CA-19.9 mucin marker.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): [CA-19.9 ... It is eliminated exclusively via bile and so any degree of cholestasis can cause levels to rise]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: According to the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST), what minimum percentage decrease in the sum of the longest diameters of target lesions is required to classify a patient's response as a 'Partial Response'?
optionExplanations: A 20% increase is the threshold for Progressive Disease; a 20% decrease does not meet the 30% threshold for Partial Response.
While a 50% decrease is a partial response, the 'at least' threshold specified in the standard criteria is 30%.
RECIST defines a Partial Response as a minimum 30% reduction in the total sum of the longest diameters of the lesions identified at baseline.
A 75% decrease exceeds the requirement; the official standard for the start of the PR category is a 30% reduction.
A 10% decrease is insufficient for any response category; it would likely fall under 'Stable Disease'.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 148 (Book Page): [Partial response (PR) At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameter (LD) of target lesions, taking as reference the baseline sum LD]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Molecular profiling of a lung adenocarcinoma specimen reveals a specific genetic alteration that predicts a high probability of response to targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy. Which alteration was likely identified?
optionExplanations: TP53 mutations are extremely common across many cancers but do not currently serve as a specific predictor for targeted TKI therapy.
In colon cancer, RAS mutations actually predict resistance to EGFR inhibitors rather than sensitivity to TKIs in lung cancer.
Loss of E-cadherin is associated with the epithelial-mesenchymal transition and invasion but is not a target for current TKI therapies.
Microsatellite instability is used primarily to predict response to checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy, not targeted TKIs.
Identification of an ALK fusion rearrangement is a 'druggable' pathway in lung cancer that indicates the patient will likely benefit from ALK inhibitors.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): [ALK fusion oncogene rearrangement – predict response to ALK inhibitor targeted therapy in lung cancer]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 24-year-old male presents with a bulky, rapidly growing midline mediastinal mass identified on a chest CT. There is no obvious primary tumor found on testicular examination. Which combination of investigations is most critical to perform next, as it may identify a highly treatable 'favorable' cancer of unknown primary?
optionExplanations: Young men with midline tumors should be screened for germ cell markers (AFP/HCG), as these cancers are highly curable even when the primary site is unknown.
Mammography and breast MRI are indicated for women with axillary adenocarcinoma, not young men with midline disease.
Colonoscopy is indicated if there are specific GI symptoms or a colorectal IHC profile, which is not the standard first step for a midline mass in a young male.
Bone marrow biopsy is helpful in suspected leukemia or lymphoma but is not the primary diagnostic pathway for a bulky midline epithelial/germ cell mass.
Sigmoidoscopy is useful for lower GI primary searches but midline distribution in a young man points specifically toward germ cell origin.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 140 (Book Page): [Men with poorly differentiated carcinoma with midline distribution T reat like germ cell cancer ... α-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) in midline disease in young men]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Biochemical Markers in Tumor Lysis Syndrome
statement: In patients at risk for Tumor Lysis Syndrome following chemotherapy, which biochemical marker is most closely correlated with total tumor bulk and serves as an indicator of increased risk for metabolic collapse?
optionExplanations: CEA is a tumor marker for colorectal and other cancers used for monitoring recurrence, not for predicting acute metabolic lysis syndromes.
TSH measures thyroid function and has no correlation with tumor bulk or the release of intracellular metabolites during lysis.
ALT is a marker of hepatocellular injury and is not a standard measure of total systemic tumor bulk or TLS risk.
LDH is released during rapid cell turnover; high baseline levels indicate a high tumor burden, placing the patient at significant risk for TLS after treatment.
Alkaline phosphatase is a marker for bone or biliary activity but does not reliably reflect total tumor bulk for TLS risk assessment.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): [pre-treatment serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) correlates with tumour bulk and may indicate increased risk.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is a significant glycoprotein used as a tumor marker for hepatocellular carcinoma and certain germ cell tumors. Where is this substance naturally found during physiological development?
options: Yolk sac and fetal liver tissue
correctOption: Yolk sac and fetal liver tissue
optionExplanations: Lymphoid follicles are associated with markers like Beta-2-microglobulin rather than alpha-fetoprotein.
The colonic mucosa is associated with Carcinoembryonic Antigen (CEA) during embryonic development, not AFP.
Pancreatic islet cells produce hormones like insulin, whereas CA-19.9 is the more common marker associated with pancreatic ductal tissue.
AFP is not associated with skeletal muscle; markers like creatine kinase are more relevant to muscle tissue.
AFP is a fetal-specific protein produced by the yolk sac and liver; its reappearance in adults suggests malignancy in those specific tissues.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): [Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) Glycoprotein found in yolk sac and fetal liver tissue.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In the TNM classification system commonly used for staging human malignancies, what does the 'M' category specifically denote?
options: Morphology of the primary tumor site
Multiplicity of lesions in the primary organ
Presence or absence of distant metastases
Marker levels in the peripheral circulation
Minimum depth of local tumor invasion
correctOption: Presence or absence of distant metastases
optionExplanations: Morphology is assessed via histopathology, not the TNM staging system, which focuses on anatomical extent.
Multiplicity of lesions is typically accounted for in the 'T' stage for some cancers but is not the 'M' category.
In the TNM system, M0 indicates no distant metastases are present, while M1 indicates their presence.
Serum tumor markers are biochemical investigations and are not part of the anatomical TNM staging descriptor.
The depth of invasion or the size of the primary tumor is designated by the 'T' (Tumor) category.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): One of the most commonly used systems is the T (tumour), N (regional lymph nodes), M (metastatic sites) approach of the International Union against Cancer (UICC, see Box 7.3).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 55-year-old male with suspected metastatic disease undergoes a Positron Emission Tomography (PET) scan. What fundamental physiological process is primarily visualized by this imaging modality?
options: Density differences between soft tissue and fluid
The integrity of the surrounding basement membrane
Metabolic activity and glucose uptake of cells
Structural anatomical disruption of normal tissue
Enhanced vascularity and blood flow in a lesion
correctOption: Metabolic activity and glucose uptake of cells
optionExplanations: Density differences are the basis for plain X-rays and computed tomography (CT) imaging.
Invasion of the basement membrane is a histological diagnosis determined via biopsy, not by PET imaging.
PET scans use radiotracers to detect areas of high metabolic activity, which is characteristic of most tumor cells.
CT and MRI are better for visualizing structural anatomical disruptions; PET focuses on metabolism.
Vascularity is typically assessed using doppler ultrasound or contrast-enhanced CT/MRI scans.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page): Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET-CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Serum tumor markers are frequently used in oncology but require careful interpretation. Which of the following conditions is a known non-malignant cause for a significant elevation of Cancer Antigen 125 (CA-125)?
options: Chronic tobacco use and nicotine exposure
Congestive heart failure and pleural effusion
correctOption: Congestive heart failure and pleural effusion
optionExplanations: COPD does not typically elevate CA-125 unless it leads to right-sided heart failure and associated ascites.
Cholestasis is a common cause of CA-19.9 elevation because it is eliminated exclusively via the bile.
Smoking is more typically associated with elevations in Carcinoembryonic Antigen (CEA) rather than CA-125.
Gastroenteritis is not a recognized cause of CA-125 elevation; inflammatory bowel disease is sometimes linked to CEA.
CA-125 is a differentiation antigen of coelomic epithelium and can be raised in heart failure or serosal effusions.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): Cancer antigen 125 (CA-125). Raised in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion or heart failure.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Management of Cancer of Unknown Primary
statement: A 68-year-old male presents with a 15-kg weight loss over 3 months, persistent upper abdominal pain, and early satiety. Physical examination reveals a palpable epigastric mass and jaundice. His heart rate is 92 bpm, BP is 115/75 mmHg, and temperature is 37.1 C. CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis shows multiple hypoenhancing lesions in the liver, small pulmonary nodules, and generalized retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, but no clear primary tumor is identified. Labs show an albumin of 28 g/L (N: 35-50) and an LDH of 550 U/L (N: 140-280). If the patient is considered fit for systemic therapy, what is the next most appropriate step to establish a diagnosis?
options: Request a whole-body PET-CT to hunt for the primary
Measure a panel of all available serum tumor markers
Obtain a core biopsy of an accessible metastatic lesion
Perform a blind colonoscopy and upper endoscopy
correctOption: Obtain a core biopsy of an accessible metastatic lesion
optionExplanations: Hunting for a primary site should be limited to investigations that help management; PET is reserved for specific cases.
Markers should be measured selectively (e.g., PSA in men with bone lesions) rather than as a broad, non-specific screen.
Chemotherapy should not be initiated without a histological diagnosis unless it is a life-threatening emergency.
In cases of unknown primary, tissue diagnosis via biopsy of a metastatic site is the most efficient diagnostic route.
Endoscopies are only indicated if there are specific localizing symptoms or radiological suspicion of a GI primary.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 140 (Book Page): If patients are fit to undergo investigations and fit enough to be considered for treatment then a core biopsy of the most accessible metastatic lesion is usually the quickest way of obtaining tissue for pathological evaluation of cancer type.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: While isotope bone scans are highly sensitive for many skeletal metastases, they may yield false-negative results in specific malignancies. In which of the following conditions is this imaging most likely to be unreliable?
options: Skeletal involvement from papillary thyroid cancer
Renal cell carcinoma with solitary cortical invasion
Multiple myeloma with lytic bone destruction
Breast cancer with mixed lytic and blastic lesions
correctOption: Multiple myeloma with lytic bone destruction
optionExplanations: Thyroid cancer can be detected via bone scan, although MRI is more sensitive for specific anatomical details.
Renal cell cancer typically produces lytic lesions, but myeloma is the classic example of bone scan failure.
Bone scans rely on osteoblast activity; myeloma suppresses this, leading to lytic lesions that do not 'light up'.
Mixed lesions usually show enough osteoblastic activity to be detected by isotope bone scanning.
Prostate cancer often produces blastic lesions which are very well-visualized on isotope bone scans.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 145 (Book Page): false-negative results occur in multiple myeloma due to suppression of osteoblast activity. Plain X-ray films or MRI scans are therefore preferred for any sites of bone pain

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A clinical investigator is assessing a patient's fitness for a new clinical trial using the ECOG performance status scale. The patient is capable of all self-care but is unable to carry out any work activities and spends approximately 6 hours of their 16-hour waking day resting in bed. What score should be assigned?
optionExplanations: Score 3 is for patients capable of only limited self-care and confined to bed/chair more than 50% of waking hours.
Score 1 involves restriction in strenuous activity but the patient is still able to carry out light work.
Score 0 is for patients who are fully active and able to carry on all usual activities without restriction.
The patient is capable of self-care but cannot work and is up for >50% of waking hours, which defines score 2.
Score 4 represents a completely disabled patient who is totally confined to a bed or chair.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): 2 - Ambulatory and capable of all self-care but unable to work. Up and about more than 50% of waking hours

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Immunohistochemical (IHC) staining of tumor tissue provides critical information for clinical decision-making. The presence of which marker on a biopsy specimen specifically indicates potential sensitivity to targeted HER2 inhibitor therapy?
optionExplanations: EMA is used to confirm the epithelial origin of a tumor but does not dictate a specific targeted therapy.
HER2 over-expression or gene amplification predicts response to drugs like trastuzumab or pertuzumab.
ER/PR positivity indicates sensitivity to hormonal manipulation, not HER2 inhibitor therapy.
CD20 is a marker for B-cell lymphomas and determines eligibility for anti-CD20 therapy like rituximab.
PSA expression suggests a prostatic origin for a metastasis but does not define 'targeted' therapy in this context.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 62-year-old female with a known history of metastatic breast cancer presents to the emergency room with a 12-hour history of escalating lower back pain and weakness. On examination, she has asymmetrical leg weakness, more pronounced on the right. Sensory loss is noted in a radicular pattern involving the L4-L5 dermatomes. Patellar and Achilles reflexes are significantly diminished bilaterally, and the plantar response is flexor. Sphincter function is currently intact. What is the most likely neurological site of involvement based on these findings?
optionExplanations: Cauda equina syndrome is characterized by asymmetrical weakness, radicular sensory loss, and absent/reduced reflexes.
Conus medullaris involvement usually shows symmetrical deficits and early sphincter loss with mixed reflex signs.
Thoracic cord compression typically presents with symmetrical weakness, increased reflexes, and extensor plantars.
Corticospinal tract lesions are upper motor neuron in nature and would cause spasticity and extensor plantar responses.
Bilateral plexopathy is rare and would not explain the radicular pattern as cleanly as cauda equina involvement.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): Cauda equina: Asymmetrical, may be mild [weakness]... Decreased knee and ankle reflexes with flexor plantar reflex... Asymmetrical, radicular pattern [sensory loss].

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A patient presents with dyspnoea, facial swelling, and distended neck veins. A mediastinal mass is suspected of causing Superior Vena Cava Obstruction (SVCO). Which investigation is specifically recommended to distinguish between extrinsic compression and intravascular thrombosis?
options: Contrast-enhanced CT scan of the thorax
correctOption: Contrast-enhanced CT scan of the thorax
optionExplanations: TTE is useful for evaluating heart function and pericardial effusions but is not the gold standard for SVCO.
PET scans show metabolic activity but do not provide the detailed vascular anatomy needed to distinguish compression from clot.
DSA is invasive; CT has largely replaced it for the initial diagnostic evaluation of superior vena cava patency.
V/Q scans are primarily used to diagnose pulmonary embolism and do not characterize mediastinal masses well.
CT thorax with contrast can visualize the vessel lumen and the surrounding mediastinal structures to determine the cause.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 143 (Book Page): The investigation of choice is a CT scan of the thorax to confirm the diagnosis and distinguish between extra- and intravascular causes.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: When performing a fine needle aspiration (FNA) of a palpable tumor or lymph node, what observation during the procedure indicates that the operator should stop sampling to avoid compromising the specimen?
options: Clear fluid entering the syringe barrel
The tumor shifting slightly during immobilization
Resistance felt as the needle enters the lesion
Visible blood appearing in the syringe hub
Patient reporting a mild stinging sensation
correctOption: Visible blood appearing in the syringe hub
optionExplanations: Clear fluid may indicate a cyst or necrotic area; the sample should still be collected for cytology.
The tumor should be immobilized by the operator's hand; slight movement does not terminate the procedure.
Resistance is often felt in fibrous tumors and is not a reason to stop the sampling procedure.
The presence of blood dilutes the cellular material and makes pathological interpretation difficult; sampling should stop.
Minor pain is common and expected; it is managed with local anesthetic rather than by stopping the FNA.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): Stop sampling if blood is seen in the syringe hub as blood reduces the quality of the sample.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 45-year-old male with a family history of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 2 (MEN 2) undergoes screening. Which serum biochemical marker is most specifically utilized to screen for and monitor medullary cell carcinoma of the thyroid in this patient?
optionExplanations: Calcitonin is the definitive marker produced by C cells and is used specifically to screen for medullary thyroid carcinoma in MEN 2 syndromes.
CA-125 is primarily associated with ovarian epithelial cancer and inflammatory serosal conditions.
Alpha-fetoprotein is primarily used for hepatocellular carcinoma and germ cell tumors, not medullary thyroid cancer.
Thyroglobulin is a marker for papillary and follicular thyroid cancers, but not for medullary thyroid cancer which arises from C cells.
Carcinoembryonic antigen is a marker for colorectal and other GI cancers; while it can be elevated in MTC, it is not the primary screening peptide.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): [Tumour marker] Calcitonin... 32-amino-acid peptide from C cells of thyroid. Used to screen for MEN 2... [Associated tumour] Medullary cell carcinoma of thyroid.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In the staging of a patient with suspected distant metastatic disease, a Positron Emission Tomography (PET) scan is combined with Computed Tomography (CT). What is the primary physiological principle that limits the sensitivity of this modality in detecting malignant lymphadenopathy?
options: The presence of structural architectural distortion
The reliance on iodine-based contrast agents
Poor anatomical resolution of the thoracic cavity
Inability to distinguish between T and N stages
Low metabolic activity in small malignant nodes
correctOption: Low metabolic activity in small malignant nodes
optionExplanations: Structural distortion is a feature of CT, but PET specifically tracks metabolic activity.
PET typically uses fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG), not standard iodine-based CT contrast, for its metabolic component.
PET-CT actually provides high resolution by fusing CT anatomy with PET metabolism.
PET-CT is excellent at distinguishing T and N stages by combining anatomy with metabolism.
PET-CT relies on high metabolic activity (glucose uptake); if a malignant node is small or lacks high uptake, it may not be detected.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page)-164: Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells... Not all tumour types are 'PET-avid' and the metabolic activity of small but malignant lymph nodes may not be detected, limiting the sensitivity of PET-CT.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: When performing staging for a patient diagnosed with rectal carcinoma or cervical cancer, which imaging modality is preferred due to its superior resolution for pelvic and soft tissue infiltration?
optionExplanations: Chest radiography is insufficient for pelvic staging and soft tissue evaluation.
CT is useful for thorax and abdomen but lacks the soft tissue contrast resolution of MRI for pelvic organs.
MRI provides the necessary high-resolution soft tissue detail required for accurate staging of pelvic malignancies like rectal and cervical cancer.
Bone scanning only evaluates skeletal metastasis, not local primary tumor invasion in the pelvis.
Ultrasound is used for liver and reproductive organs but is not the gold standard for rectal or cervical staging.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page): Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. It is widely employed for the staging of rectal, cervical and prostate cancers.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 68-year-old heavy smoker presents with a 3 cm mass in the right upper lobe of the lung. A CT scan shows several enlarged hilar lymph nodes on the same side. Using the TNM classification system, how should the physician categorize the finding of enlarged regional lymph nodes that cannot be further assessed without invasive sampling?
optionExplanations: NX is the specific designation used when regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed or have not been evaluated.
N0 would mean there is definitive evidence of no nodal involvement.
N1 requires definitive proof of involvement in specific regional nodes, which is not yet established if they are only noted as 'enlarged' on CT without assessment.
M0 refers to the absence of distant metastases, not the status of regional nodes.
T2 refers to the primary tumor size/depth, not the lymph node status.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): TNM classification... Increased involvement of nodes... NX: Not assessed; N0: No nodal involvement; N1, N2/3: Increases in involvement.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: During a Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA) of a palpable neck mass, the clinician makes multiple rapid passes through the lesion with a needle and syringe. Which observation is the definitive indication to immediately stop the sampling procedure to maintain the quality of the specimen?
options: Appearance of blood in the syringe hub
Visualization of solid material in the needle
Changing the angle of the needle entry
Achievement of a negative pressure vacuum
correctOption: Appearance of blood in the syringe hub
optionExplanations: Hemodilution significantly degrades the cytological quality, making blood in the hub the standard clinical trigger to stop.
Solid material in the needle is often the goal of FNA (cellular yield).
Mild discomfort is common; as long as it is tolerated, the procedure continues.
Varying angles is part of the standard technique to ensure representative sampling.
Negative pressure is required to aspirate cells; its presence does not require stopping.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): [Box 7.5] Stop sampling if blood is seen in the syringe hub as blood reduces the quality of the sample.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 72-year-old patient with metastatic lung cancer is evaluated in the oncology clinic. The patient is capable of all self-care but is unable to carry out any work activities and spends approximately 40% of their waking hours resting in a chair. What is the most appropriate ECOG performance status for this patient?
optionExplanations: Grade 1 involves restriction in strenuous activity but the patient is still able to do light work.
Grade 3 applies when the patient is confined to a bed or chair for more than 50% of waking hours.
Grade 0 means fully active and able to carry out all pre-disease activities without restriction.
Grade 2 applies to patients who are capable of all self-care but unable to work, and are up more than 50% of the day.
Grade 4 means the patient is completely disabled and totally confined to a bed or chair.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): [Box 7.6] 2: Ambulatory and capable of all self-care but unable to work. Up and about more than 50% of waking hours.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In a patient with newly diagnosed breast cancer, immunohistochemical (IHC) staining is performed on the biopsy specimen. The finding of HER2 receptor positivity is of critical clinical value primarily because it predicts response to which management strategy?
optionExplanations: Mastectomy is a surgical decision based on local extent and genetics (BRCA), not IHC markers like HER2.
Radiotherapy is used for local control regardless of HER2 status in most protocols.
HER2 positivity is a predictive biomarker for response to HER2 inhibitors like trastuzumab.
Selective estrogen receptor modulators (like tamoxifen) are used for ER+ disease.
Aromatase inhibitors are used for estrogen-receptor positive (ER+) tumors, not specifically HER2+.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Management of Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP)
statement: A 24-year-old male presents with a large midline mediastinal mass and multiple lung nodules. A primary site cannot be identified on initial imaging. Which combination of investigations is most vital to perform urgently as they may lead to a diagnosis and rapid initiation of potentially curative therapy?
options: Isotope bone scan and skeletal survey
Colonoscopy and fecal occult blood testing
optionExplanations: Bone scans evaluate metastatic spread but do not identify the primary tumor type in this acute presentation.
Rectal biopsy is used for suspected anogenital or colorectal primary, not midline mediastinal disease.
Midline tumors in young men are highly suspicious for germ cell tumors; AFP and hCG are essential for rapid diagnosis.
Breast imaging is appropriate for women with axillary nodes, not young men with midline disease.
Colonoscopy is indicated only if GI symptoms are present; midline disease in young men points to germ cell origins.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 140 (Book Page)-169: [Box 7.11] Tumor markers... alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) in midline disease in young men... [Box 7.12] Men with poorly differentiated carcinoma with midline distribution: Treat like germ cell cancer.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In patients undergoing treatment for bulky, chemosensitive malignancies like high-grade lymphoma, regular monitoring of serum biochemistry is essential. Which pre-treatment laboratory value is the most significant indicator of high tumor bulk and increased risk for Tumor Lysis Syndrome?
optionExplanations: CRP is an inflammatory marker and does not specifically quantify tumor burden as effectively as LDH.
LDH is released during cell turnover; high levels before treatment signal a large tumor burden prone to lysis.
Sodium levels are more often associated with SIADH paraneoplastic syndromes, not tumor bulk lysis.
Bilirubin levels reflect liver function or biliary obstruction, not global tumor burden.
Low albumin is a poor prognostic factor but does not specifically track tumor bulk for lysis risk.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 143 (Book Page): Elevated serum potassium may be the earliest biochemical marker but pre-treatment serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) correlates with tumour bulk and may indicate increased risk [of tumor lysis syndrome].

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 65-year-old patient with back pain is suspected of having skeletal metastases. While an isotope bone scan is highly sensitive for many cancers, it is known to produce false-negative results in which specific malignancy due to the suppression of osteoblast activity?
optionExplanations: Renal cell carcinoma usually produces lytic lesions that can be seen, though MRI is often better.
Prostate cancer often produces blastic lesions which are very well visualized on bone scans.
Breast cancer can produce mixed lytic/blastic lesions and is usually detected on bone scan.
Multiple Myeloma is primarily osteolytic and suppresses osteoblasts; since bone scans rely on osteoblast activity, they are often negative.
Thyroid cancer metastases are generally detectable on isotope bone scans if they are osteoblastic.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 145 (Book Page): The most sensitive way of detecting bone metastases is by isotope bone scan... false-negative results occur in multiple myeloma due to suppression of osteoblast activity.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Biochemical tumor markers for germ cell malignancies
statement: A 24-year-old male presents with a large midline abdominal mass and significantly elevated serum levels of a specific glycoprotein. Histopathological analysis suggests a non-seminomatous germ cell tumor. Which of the following tumor markers is most commonly associated with this specific diagnosis and used for monitoring therapy?
optionExplanations: Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is a classic marker for non-seminomatous germ cell tumors and hepatocellular carcinoma.
Calcitonin is specifically used for medullary cell carcinoma of the thyroid.
CA-125 is primarily used for monitoring epithelial ovarian cancer.
Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) is typically associated with colorectal and gastrointestinal cancers.
Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) is specific for prostate tissue and malignancies.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) Glycoprotein found in yolk sac and fetal liver tissue... Ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (80%), testicular teratoma (80%), hepatocellular cancer (50%)

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Imaging modality selection for pelvic malignancies
statement: In the clinical staging of a patient with newly diagnosed cervical or rectal carcinoma, which imaging modality is preferred for its high resolution and ability to accurately define pelvic involvement?
optionExplanations: Bone scans are specific for detecting skeletal metastases and provide no information on local pelvic primary tumor staging.
Ultrasound is useful for characterising liver or renal lesions but lacks the resolution required for formal pelvic cancer staging.
PET is used primarily for metabolic assessment of distant metastases rather than local pelvic staging.
CT is excellent for thorax and abdomen staging but has lower soft-tissue resolution for pelvic organs compared to MRI.
MRI provides superior soft-tissue contrast, making it the gold standard for pelvic staging in rectal and cervical cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. It is widely employed for the staging of rectal, cervical and prostate cancers.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Early biochemical markers of Tumor Lysis Syndrome
statement: A 45-year-old patient with bulky high-grade lymphoma begins induction chemotherapy. Within the first 24 hours, the medical team monitors for metabolic complications. Which of the following biochemical findings is often the earliest indicator of tumor lysis syndrome in such cases?
optionExplanations: Hyperkalaemia occurs rapidly as intracellular potassium is released during the massive lysis of malignant cells.
Serum phosphate levels typically increase, not decrease, during tumor lysis syndrome.
Uric acid levels rise as purines are metabolised, potentially causing renal crystal precipitation.
Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels are high as a marker of tumor bulk, but potassium is the earliest electrolyte marker.
Calcium levels typically drop (hypocalcaemia) due to precipitation with the released phosphate.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): Cellular destruction results in the release of potassium, phosphate, nucleic acids and purines... Elevated serum potassium may be the earliest biochemical marker

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Management of Malignant Spinal Cord Compression
statement: A 52-year-old woman with a history of treated breast cancer presents with a two-week history of worsening mid-back pain that radiates in a band-like fashion around her chest. The pain is exacerbated by coughing and lying flat. On examination, she has 4/5 power in both lower limbs, hyperreflexia, and a sensory level at T8. What is the most appropriate next step in the diagnostic and immediate management of this patient?
options: Ultrasound of the back and morphine titrations
Urgent whole spine MRI and dexamethasone
Plain spinal X-ray and surgical referral
Thoracic spine CT and urgent radiotherapy
correctOption: Urgent whole spine MRI and dexamethasone
optionExplanations: Ultrasound is not a diagnostic tool for spinal cord pathology; while analgesia is needed, it is not the definitive diagnostic step.
The presentation strongly suggests spinal cord compression, requiring urgent whole-spine MRI for confirmation and steroids to reduce oedema.
Bone scans identify areas of increased turnover but do not provide the anatomical detail needed to diagnose cord compression.
Plain X-rays may show bony lesions but cannot confirm spinal cord compression or assess the neural elements.
MRI is the gold standard over CT for cord compression; radiotherapy is a treatment but requires confirmation and steroids first.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 141 (Book Page): Malignant spinal cord compression... Confirm diagnosis with urgent MRI scan of whole spine. Administer high-dose glucocorticoids: Dexamethasone 16 mg IV or oral stat

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A patient is evaluated for suitability for systemic chemotherapy.
